subject: Acme MSA — exit playbook / term & renewal trade-offs
messages:
From: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Sanders <jill.sanders@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MSA redline (term + auto-renew / TFC)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for sending your draft. Attached is Acme's annotated MSA (ACME_MSA_vAC_redline.docx) — we highlighted a couple of must-haves for our GC:
- Auto-renew capped at single renewal term; any subsequent renewal requires written consent.
- Minimum 120-day advance notice for non-renewal/termination.
- Termination for convenience allowed for pilot accounts with 60-day notice but limited to pro-rated fees; we asked for a transition assistance clause (30 days).

I realize some of this is higher than standard, but this is a procurement must for our internal sign-off. If Redwood can offer stronger transition support and a limited credit in lieu of a long notice, that would help.

Attaching redline and a short summary for clarity. Can we aim to resolve the T&C items this week?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Greene
Senior Sourcing Manager — Acme Procurement

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline (term + auto-renew / TFC)

Team — looping you in. Acme is pushing 120-day notice and a pilot carve-out for TFC.

Commercial trade-offs I want us to consider before we respond:
- Notice window: 120d vs our standard 90d. Longer window increases potential unpaid runout and support costs.
- Auto-renew: single-rollover cap is reasonable; we can offer a single automatic renewal then manual.
- TFC for pilots: they want low friction to exit; offering 30 days transition + pro-rated refund might be staged with a small onboarding refund.

Action items:
- Aditya / Laura — can you propose redline language that:
  1) Limits notice to 90 days with a compromise path to 120 if Acme signs a 12-mo paid commitment, or if they require 120d we request a partial runout fee cap (e.g., no more than 1 month of fees).
  2) Allow TFC for pilots but cap liability and require a handback plan (data deletion timeline + transition assistance for up to 30 days).
- Marissa — commercial okay with a limited onboarding credit (we could offer 10% of first quarter ARR or fixed $X) to offset their discomfort? If yes, what number do we give?

Tom / Jill — we want to be responsive. Can we set a 30-minute call Thursday to close the remaining items after we send a counter-redline?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of GTM — Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline (term + auto-renew / TFC)

Quick commercial read: we should prioritize sale velocity but protect gross margin. My recommendation:
- Offer 90-day notice by default. If Acme signs a 12-month committed order form at a target TCV (we can reference Tier A pricing band), escalate to 120-day notice as concession.
- For pilots: grant TFC with 30-day notice but cap liability to: refund of unused prepaid months OR a fixed cap equal to 1x monthly committed spend (whichever is lower).
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit of $12,500 (or 10% of Q1 ARR) — whichever they prefer; this is small and buys flexibility.

I've attached a short trade-off spreadsheet that models runout exposure at different notice windows. Please review — we can iterate language after legal drafts their redline.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: MATP_acme_term_tradeoffs.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme.com>, Jill Sanders <jill.sanders@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline (term + auto-renew / TFC)

Vivek / team — see inline suggested language below (we'll produce a tracked-redline doc once you confirm the direction):

On 120d notice: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice to the other party; provided that if Customer has executed an Order Form committing to twelve (12) months or more of Services, the notice period shall be one hundred twenty (120) days."

On auto-renew: "Any Order Form shall automatically renew for one successive term equal to the expiring Order Form term unless either party provides written notice at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term; any additional renewal shall require mutual written agreement."

On TFC for pilots: "Customer may terminate a Pilot Order Form for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. In the event of such termination Customer's sole remedy shall be a prorated refund of any prepaid fees for the unused portion of the then-current billing cycle, or, at Provider's election, a credit in the amount of one (1) month of committed fees, provided that Provider's aggregate liability under this Section shall not exceed the lesser of (i) the total fees paid for the Pilot period or (ii) one (1) month's committed fees."

Notes / next steps: 1) If you approve this approach I'll post a tracked redline against ACME_MSA_vAC_redline.docx and include the compromise credit numbers. 2) Marissa — please confirm the onboarding credit value you prefer so legal can bake it into a commercial paragraph (we can phrase as "one-time credit" on execution). 3) Suggest a 30-min sync with Acme on Thu 11/18 to walk the compromise.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Counsel — Redwood Inference
